body.statement:
There is a terminating quantifier-elimination procedure for first-order
formulas over real closed fields; in particular, a formula with real algebraic
coefficients can be converted effectively to an equivalent quantifier-free
Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions.

source.locator: Tarski, A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry, quantifier-elimination decision theorem
source.verbatim_statement: In this monograph we present a method for deciding on the truth of sentences of the elementary algebra of real numbers. By a decision method is meant a method by which one can always decide in a finite number of steps.

attestation.note: Tarski, A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry, Introduction pp. 1-2 and Section 2; exact text checked against the publicly available 1951 book transcription and RAND R-109 record on 2026-09-13. Section 2 implements the method by eliminating quantified variables into equations and inequalities.

body.justification: Termination of the exact algebraic procedure is a classical real-algebraic result.
body.consumer: It decides finite-lift membership, projections, endpoint characterizations, and endpoint inclusion.
